question.problem:
The change-of-coordinates matrix from $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ to $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\}$ is given below. Find $[x]_{B}$ given that $x=5{c}_{1}+12{c}_{2}.$

$$
{P}_{B\to C}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change-of-coordinates formula in the form

$$
[\,x\,]_{B}={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C}.
$$

First, we need to find the change-of-coordinates matrix ${P}_{C\to B}$ from $C$ to $B.$ To do that, we compute the inverse of ${P}_{B\to C}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{C\to B} & ={P}_{B\to C}^{-1} \\  & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 3-1\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that since $x=5{c}_{1}+12{c}_{2},$ we obtain 

$$
[x]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 12\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Now, we compute $[\,x\,]_{B}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}[\,x\,]_{B} & ={P}_{C\to B}[\,x\,]_{C} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
